item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Through the Gates of Hell: American Injustice at Guantánamo Bay — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — Van Vleck House & Gardens
item.description:
Author and human rights attorney Joshua Colangelo-Bryan joins us to discuss his acclaimed book, Through the Gates of Hell, which recounts his experience representing a detainee at Guantánamo Bay and the unlikely friendship the two men developed through their shared pursuit of justice. Colangelo-Bryan will be joined in conversation by John Torpey, Presidential Professor of Sociology and History and Director of the Ralph Bunche Institute for International Studies at the CUNY Graduate Center and Montclair resident. $15 MEMBER ADMISSION | $20 GENERAL ADMISSION. item.title: 2026 Jersey City Art and Studio Tour (JCAST) — Thu Oct 1, 4:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Creative Side JC presents the 2026 Jersey City Art & Studio Tour (JCAST), the 37th edition from October 1st to the 4th, with the theme, Unbounded Nature. JCAST is a robust city-wide series featuring 150+ arts venues (in the 6 wards) presenting visual art including 200+ artist studios with 5 signature exhibitions to showcase both the best, diverse, and inclusive works of Jersey City artists, not just limited to fine art and with performance, music, poetry, and film. It begins with a Kick-Off Opening event featuring the Jersey City Legend Awards and features 100+ art gallery and art exhibitions, 50+ poetry, music and film events, 25+ art workshops for kids and adults, 10+ art, murals, bus and walking tours, throughout the city, and concludes with a closing party. item.title: Frame Your Space -- Gallery Opening — Thu Oct 1, 6:00 PM — Ria X Gallery
item.description:
An intimate evening at Ricardo Roig’s new gallery in Montclair, where art, design, and home come together in a truly personalized experience. Bring a photo of a room or wall in your home that feels unfinished, and sit down with renowned artist Ricardo Roig, a second-generation professional framer Ria Mulvey, independent curator and art advisor Larissa Reick and Design Director at Mulvey Custom Homes Mika Cali for thoughtful guidance on selecting artwork that complements your space. From scale and color to framing and placement, you’ll gain expert insight into how to create a home that feels collected and intentional. Following your consultation, enjoy a selection of wine, champagne, and beer as you continue exploring the gallery, connect with fellow design enthusiasts, and mingle with the evening’s creative collaborators. item.title: PAULINA OLIVARES | MEMORIES — Thu Oct 1, 6:00 PM — Gallery491
item.description: Opening Reception: Thursday, October 1, 2026 6:00 pm – 8:00 pm Show Runs: October 1 – December 18, 2026 MONTCLAIR, NJ — This October, Gallery491 presents Memories, a new exhibition by artist Paulina Olivares that invites viewers into a deeply personal, dreamlike world. On view October 1 through December 18, 2026, the show offers a quiet, intimate look at how the past stays with us, and how art can hold space for both its weight and its beauty. Memories offers an intimate look at the relationship between personal history and artistic expression. Olivares’s work speaks to the resilience of the human spirit and the possibility of transforming difficult or painful memories into spaces of beauty, reflection, and renewal. Born in Chile and now based in Bloomfield, NJ, Olivares holds a BFA from Parsons School of Design and a master’s in education from Kean University. item.title: Gina Miele, "Italian Folklore Rituals, Celebrations, and Ancient Traditions" — Thu Oct 1, 7:00 PM — Watchung Booksellers
item.description:
In conversation with Mark Rotella, Director of The Coccia Institute for the Italian Experience in America. Tickets are $5 and include a 10% discount on the book purchased at the event. Explore the rich and mystical world of Italian folk traditions, where saints walked with witches and magic was found in the smallest of items. Did you grow up hearing stories of “the evil eye?” Or perhaps, you’ve always wondered why Italian culture lights candles for saints. In Italian Folklore, Dr. Gina Miele weaves scholarly expertise and cultural passion into a rich tapestry of storytelling, history, and ritual practice to explore folk traditions from the old world. This beautifully illustrated, comprehensive book, told through fictional stories of everyday Italians, examines and honors Italy’s mystical heritage, where saints, healers, and peasants kept spiritual traditions alive through daily acts and seasonal rites. item.title: CSAM Science Teaching Program - How Can I Apply To The Teacher Certification Program? — Mon Oct 5, 2:00 PM — SCHM 329 (CSAM Innovation and Design Lab)
item.description:
Join the CSAM Science Teaching Program for our next meeting on Monday, October 5, at 2:00 p.m. in SCHM 329, the CSAM Design and Innovation Lab! Our student leadership team will welcome Ms. Hiba Khalil, Pre-Program Advisor in the Center for Student Success and Educator Excellence within Montclair State University’s College for Education and Engaged Learning. Ms. Khalil will discuss how to prepare for and apply to teacher certification programs, helping students understand the next steps toward becoming a teacher. Whether you are just beginning to explore science teaching or are already committed to pursuing certification, come with your questions and connect with a supportive community of future science educators.
Hosted by: College of Science and Mathematics (CSAM)
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12821245
Source: Montclair State University

item.title: Bible Study (Guild Room) — Tue Oct 6, 12:30 PM — Guild Room
item.description:
The Tuesday Daytime Bible Study Group meets weekly in the Guild Room, offering opportunities to explore faith, the Bible, Christian history, Union Church, and societal concerns. Beginning September 15, the group will read and discuss The False White Gospel: Rejecting Christian Nationalism by Rev. Jim Wallis. Later in the year, the group will also explore non-canonical biblical texts with Rev. Katrina. Newcomers are welcome – come join the conversation!
Source: Union Congregational Church
